title: Default and saved settings show as separate groups in the reports
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to the build under test as a dispatcher whose role has Work Orders view and Work Orders create and edit (check: Settings > Roles & Permissions > open the role > on the Work Orders card, View and Create & Edit are both ticked. The Admin role has both).
  2. In the top bar, choose the location you test in (e.g. "Heavy Duty"). Every technician and work order below belongs to this location.
  3. Use a desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide (the display switcher only shows at 1024 px and wider).
  4. You can open Google Analytics for the property the QA build reports to, at Admin > DebugView. The QA build runs analytics in debug mode, so each event appears in DebugView within a few seconds under your user. If you cannot open DebugView, the event checks in this case cannot be done by hand: write "not checked by hand" in the result comment and pass or fail on what you can see on the Work Orders page.
  5. Event names to look for in DebugView: work_orders_display_view (a display was shown), work_orders_field_load and work_orders_density_load (the fields and density you have, once per display per session), work_orders_field_toggle and work_orders_density_change (a saved change).
  6. A brand-new user who has never opened Work Orders (Settings > Staff > add, e.g. "ZZAUTOTEST Newbie", with Work Orders View).
  7. Your dispatcher has chosen a density (e.g. Comfortable) in an earlier session.
  8. You can open the Story 12 reports in Google Analytics (built and kept by Milos Vasic).
custom_steps:
1. Sign in as ZZAUTOTEST Newbie, open Work Orders and click Board View. Read the source on the display, field and density events in DebugView.
  2. Sign in as your dispatcher, open Work Orders and click Board View. Read the same sources.
  3. The next day (reports are not live), open the Story 12 reports and find the density and field reports for the test date.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the events show source default.
  • Step 2: the density event shows source saved (Comfortable).
  • Step 3: the reports show default, saved and fallback as separate groups, with ZZAUTOTEST Newbie under default and your dispatcher's density under saved.
  • A fallback (a setting that could not be loaded) cannot be caused by hand. Write "fallback: not checked by hand" in the result comment.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10593 (Story 12, Google Analytics for display and field usage); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S12-R12, Story 12 report owner, read 8 Oct 2026. Event names and timing: SV-10593 comments by Slavcho Mitrov and Milos Vasic, 6 Oct 2026 (the agreed GA4 event table); earlier event contract on Review Decisions page 853901313 (29 Sep 2026) uses older names.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S12-R12: “Separate default, saved, and fallback preference cohorts in reports.”
  • Story 12 report owner: “Milos Vasic owns building and maintaining the reports in S12-R4 and S12-R10 to S12-R12. Engineering’s part of this story ends at sending the events; Story 12 is complete when both are done.”
